original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 4 Processor Upgrade enum for every expected processor socket accurately reports the platform's physical socket/upgrade-interface design and remains unchanged after reboot; no processor replacement is part of this case.
original_method: Capture complete raw and decoded Type 4 records, bind each Processor Upgrade byte to its socket/handle, normalize only defined enum values, compare with the approved board/socket design, reboot and repeat while performing no physical CPU work.
manual_activity: A user approves the expected socket-interface enum and reboot plan. Metadata collection, enum decoding, mapping and persistence comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Approved Processor Upgrade enum for each socket
Platform board/socket design and expected Type 4 mapping
SMBIOS-version-aware enum table and reserved/unknown-value policy
Approved reboot, service-impact and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: This is read-only metadata validation; do not remove, install or reseat a processor and do not alter socket hardware or firmware.
Preserve the raw enum byte, decoded label, record handle and socket designation; grep fragments can associate a value with the wrong socket.
Do not translate an unknown/reserved enum into a guessed connector type.
Confirm the approved platform design rather than deriving acceptance solely from current CPU presence.
Stop on unsupported enum, missing/duplicate mapping, unexpected drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete Type 4 raw/decoded data, map Processor Upgrade values to sockets, compare with the approved mechanical design before/after reboot and preserve evidence.
Do not perform a physical upgrade, change firmware or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the expected processor socket/upgrade enum and treatment of legacy or unknown values.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The target label is correct, but grep suppresses errors and loses the raw enum, full record and per-socket association.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw and decoded Type 4 records, retain each handle/socket/Processor Upgrade byte and validate defined enums against the approved physical socket design.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Processor Upgrade metadata scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the raw Processor Upgrade enum with the applicable SMBIOS table, bind it to each expected socket and compare it with authoritative board/socket documentation before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, board revision, CPU/socket topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Processor Upgrade enumeration, approved platform board/socket specification and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes enum provenance, raw value and socket-level design comparison explicit while excluding physical processor work.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; it validates the complete metadata set rather than a filtered label.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved enum and physical socket design.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The enum describes the physical upgrade interface, not whether a particular replacement CPU is electrically or firmware compatible.

project_override_considerations: A project can approve different socket connector enums by board revision or socket position, but must retain the exact topology and may not interpret this case as authorization for a CPU swap.
expected_evidence: Approved per-socket upgrade-interface baseline, board revision, enum table and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 records with handle/socket/raw enum/decoded label
Complete post-reboot capture and per-socket persistence comparison
Engineer verdict; no claim that a physical processor upgrade was performed

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The field name denotes a capability enum, and the generic procedure/criteria can be satisfied through read-only metadata validation without a physical upgrade.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The enum is safely readable; missing expected platform value is a project readiness input.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw enum, complete records and per-socket mechanical-design validation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Preserves the important no-physical-upgrade boundary while correcting the classification to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under the locked V3.1 rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates connector capability metadata from CPU compatibility or replacement activity.

review_improvement: Prevents a misleading physical-upgrade interpretation and prevents a decoded label from masking a reserved raw value or wrong socket association.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once the expected board/socket enum is approved, all core collection, decoding, mapping and reboot comparison steps are software-controlled and read-only.
